UserPreference.title: UserPreference
UserPreference.description: Stores user-specific settings and configurations for the TempAlert application, including alert thresholds and notification preferences.

id.description: Unique identifier for the UserPreference entity.

externalAuthId.description: Identifier from the external authentication system (e.g., Firebase User ID) to link these preferences to a specific authenticated user.

alertEmail.description: The email address where alert notifications should be sent.

temperatureThreshold.description: The temperature value that, if exceeded, will trigger an alert.

unitPreference.description: The preferred unit of temperature measurement (e.g., 'Celsius', 'Fahrenheit') for display and threshold settings.

createdAt.description: Timestamp indicating when the user's preferences were first created.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp indicating when the user's preferences were last updated.

TemperatureMeasurement.title: TemperatureMeasurement
TemperatureMeasurement.description: Records individual temperature readings over time for historical tracking and real-time display.

id.description: Unique identifier for the TemperatureMeasurement entity.

userPreferenceId.description: Reference to the UserPreference entity that these measurements are associated with. (Relationship: UserPreference 1:N TemperatureMeasurement)

unit.description: The unit of temperature measurement for this reading (e.g., 'Celsius', 'Fahrenheit').

timestamp.description: The exact date and time the temperature was measured.

AlertEvent.title: AlertEvent
AlertEvent.description: Logs details of each instance an alert was triggered and sent due to temperature exceeding a configured threshold.

id.description: Unique identifier for the AlertEvent entity.

userPreferenceId.description: Reference to the UserPreference entity whose threshold configuration triggered this alert. (Relationship: UserPreference 1:N AlertEvent)

triggeredValue.description: The temperature value that caused the alert to be triggered.

thresholdSetAtTrigger.description: The temperature threshold value that was configured at the moment this alert was triggered.

unitAtTrigger.description: The unit of temperature measurement relevant to the alert (e.g., 'Celsius', 'Fahrenheit').

alertEmailSentTo.description: The email address to which the alert notification was sent.

timestamp.description: The exact date and time the alert was generated and sent.

definition.description: Stores user-specific settings and preferences. Each user has a single UserPreference document with the fixed ID 'settings'. The 'externalAuthId' field within the document must match the 'userId' in the path and 'request.auth.uid' for robust authorization.

firestore.reasoning:
The recommended Firestore structure for the TempAlert application prioritizes robust security, scalability, and debuggability by adhering to the core design principles, especially Authorization Independence and Structural Segregation. 

1.  **Authorization Independence (Denormalization for Rules):**
    *   `UserPreference`: Each user's settings are stored in `/users/{userId}/settings`. The document's `externalAuthId` field, which stores the Firebase Authentication UID (`request.auth.uid`), acts as the denormalized owner identifier. This allows rules to verify `request.auth.uid == userId && resource.data.externalAuthId == userId` without relying on slow and insecure `get()` operations.
    *   `TemperatureMeasurement` and `AlertEvent`: These entities are related to a `UserPreference` but for security, they must directly indicate their owner. To achieve this, an additional `ownerUserId` field (of type `string`) MUST be added to both `TemperatureMeasurement` and `AlertEvent` schemas. This `ownerUserId` field will store the `request.auth.uid` of the user who owns the parent `UserPreference`. This denormalization means that security rules for these collections can simply check `request.auth.uid == userId && resource.data.ownerUserId == userId`, ensuring authorization is self-contained within each document and its path, thus eliminating the need for `get()` calls.

2.  **Structural Segregation (Homogeneous Security Posture):**
    *   All data (`UserPreference`, `TemperatureMeasurement`, `AlertEvent`) is strictly private to the authenticated user. By nesting all user-specific data under `/users/{userId}/...`, we ensure that all documents within these user-specific subcollections (`settings`, `temperatureMeasurements`, `alertEvents`) share the exact same security requirements: only the owner (`request.auth.uid == userId`) can access them. This simplifies security rules significantly, moving complexity from rule logic to the data structure itself.

3.  **QAPs (Rules are not Filters):**
    *   The hierarchical path structure (`/users/{userId}/...`) naturally enables secure and efficient `list` operations. When a client requests data from a user's subcollection (e.g., `/users/{request.auth.uid}/temperatureMeasurements`), the `userId` wildcard in the path directly corresponds to `request.auth.uid`. Security rules can then simply `allow list: if request.auth.uid == userId;`. The additional check on the denormalized `externalAuthId` (for `UserPreference`) or `ownerUserId` (for `TemperatureMeasurement` and `AlertEvent`) within each document provides an extra layer of data integrity, guaranteeing that only truly owned documents are returned, even if a query path was somehow manipulated. This ensures that the client's query is implicitly filtered by ownership before any data is returned, upholding the QAP principle.
